headline: AI is letting more Chinese entrepreneurs run businesses alone or in tiny teams, and larger firms are trying to follow, CNA reports.
score_reason: Kept at 5: a broad feature with real examples, but the gains are self-reported by the people and companies interviewed.
importance_line: Workers in services such as video and research could face fewer jobs while solo founders gain, but the figures are self-reported and the Ant Group executive expects more jobs in the long run.
summary: CNA reports that AI is helping a growing number of one-person companies in China, reportedly more than 16 million by June 2025, do work that once took staff; one video producer says jobs that took three days now take about three hours and, by his own estimate, his income is 60 to 80 per cent above what his seven-person studio earned. Ant Group's technology arm says its AI assistant writes investment research reports in minutes, but an executive says staff resistance is the main obstacle for larger firms.
notes: Full CNA text read. Numbers are interviewees' estimates or company claims.
